text:
maya: FYI — noticed p99 tail blips (~120-180ms) for tiny-window fastpath during slab compaction yesterday. correlates with merge phases.

oliver: do we block the enqueue hotpath or just serialize the kv updates? which lock?

maya: enqueue is blocked on the slab mutex while pointer reconciliation runs. most tenants reroute but affinity dents p99 for a few customers.

sasha: could we do a lock-free swap + bg reconcile? that usually helps but it can surface double-enqueue for late-joins.

pranav: I prototyped swap+bg; reduced tail but introduced race for requests arriving during the swap. needs a handshake marker.

jen: forwarding new arrivals off-slab is another option but that costs extra routing and may hurt p50. trade p50 vs p99 here. what SLO do we target?

maya: aim is stable p50 and p99 < 100ms for small reqs — customers started seeing errors.

oliver: brainstorm options: (A) cooperative compaction that yields frequently, (B) staged swap + forwarding marker, (C) copy-on-write background compaction off fastpath, (D) prefix-reserve for late joins.

sasha: (A) looks lowest risk: yield the compactor every N ops so enqueue interleaves. con: slower compaction and more fragmentation for a while.

pranav: make yields adaptive: tie them to live slab_rps rather than a fixed op count so busy slabs yield sooner. also add a short exponential backoff to avoid thrashing.

maya: agreed. we can implement metric-driven yield: if slab_rps > threshold -> break out and reschedule. emit telemetry (compaction_duration, yields, slab_rps).

jen: (D) prefix-reserve sounds intriguing: reserve a tiny header window so late-join enqueues bypass merge until reconcile finishes. less routing, more bookkeeping. downside: short underutilization.

oliver: prefix-reserve avoids per-request redirect, but needs tight accounting to not starve the compactor. could be opt-in per-tenant.

maya: proposed plan: 1) ship metric-driven cooperative compaction with adaptive yields, 2) add telemetry fields (compaction_reason, yield_count, pre-move_count, slab_rps), 3) prototype prefix-reserve as an opt-in experiment.

sasha: add e2e repro harness that simulates a high-affinity tenant hitting a slab during compaction and asserts p99 < 100ms. we'll need both microbench and canary.

jen: also add dashboard chart: compaction yields vs p99 tail over time. quick check to validate hypothesis. :eyes: 

pranav: small note: when yielding, we could opportunistically move a handful of pending enqueues to sibling slabs (cheap rehash) to reduce affinity pressure. might help steady the tail.

maya: that increases complexity but we can gate behind a flag for the canary.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout of compactor-change -> eng-runtime/canary at 03:00 UTC.

sasha: I'll pair with maya for the canary checklist and run the harness.

maya: I'll open an RFC follow-up with the design choices, telemetry PR, and the canary checklist. thanks everyone.

oliver: sounds good — :thumbsup:
